stories.title: Attacks and blockade enforcement around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November, with a Sinokor VLCC struck and four crew injured amid what trade press describes as near-daily Iranian attacks on foreign-flag shipping. The IMO has called on all parties to respect seafarer safety, citing at least 25 seafarer deaths since February.
stories.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and crew-safety objections raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings and shrink the pool of willing owners, and the crisis is linked to an estimated $95bn of extra industry fuel spend.
stories.latest: Four injured on a Sinokor VLCC as multiple tankers were attacked in Hormuz; IMO issued a seafarer safety appeal; a report says bunker prices have fallen up to 20% in under two weeks on hopes of an easing of the conflict.
sources: Four injured on Sinokor VLCC as multiple tankers attacked in Hormuz
IMO Calls for All Parties in Hormuz Crisis to Respect Seafarer Safety

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while the dark fleet is described as a parallel fleet that has tripled since 2022. The US Treasury may now allow companies to buy sanctioned vessels and return them to legitimate trade on a case-by-case basis.
stories.why_it_matters: Registry fraud and designations force charterers and insurers to re-verify documents and positions; a licensing route back to legitimate trade could return tonnage to the compliant fleet.
stories.latest: Report that the US Treasury may permit purchases of sanctioned tankers on a case-by-case basis.
sources: US Treasury may allow purchase of sanctioned tankers on case basis

stories.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
stories.what: A reported US-Russia arrangement on extra diesel for the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a ban on most diesel exports to end-January. A tanker carrying Russian diesel that had signalled the US has now turned around off the US East Coast.
stories.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment.
stories.latest: The tanker made a U-turn about 400 nautical miles off New York, compounding uncertainty over North American deliveries.
sources: Russian Diesel Tanker Makes U-Turn After Heading to U.S.

stories.title: Wave of tanker newbuilding orders
stories.what: COSCO Shipping Development has ordered 16 VLCCs worth 13.43 billion yuan ($2.01bn) from China State Shipbuilding Group, and Teekay Tankers has ordered four more newbuildings in China and South Korea, lifting its programme to six ships worth $525.9m.
stories.why_it_matters: Large orderbook additions change future crude and product tanker supply and shape secondhand values and recycling decisions.
stories.latest: COSCO's 16-VLCC order and Teekay's four-ship order reported today, alongside reports of rising ship recycling demand and a 61% jump in October tanker secondhand sales to 82 vessels.
sources: Teekay Tankers doubles down on newbuilds with four-ship deal
Tankers In High Demand During October
Demand Rising in the Ship Recycling Markets

stories.title: US port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships
stories.what: The US administration has formally extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue.
stories.why_it_matters: The fees, if reinstated, would change the cost of deploying Chinese-built tonnage into US trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.

stories.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
stories.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, and Russia says its forces hit three cargo vessels it claims carried military goods for Ukraine, plus two electricity substations.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
sources: Webinar: Navigating the danger zone: How to protect your fleet from GPS attacks
